userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: Ford Foundation has title, copyright and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them.

The Rockefeller Archive Center has authority to grant permission to cite and publish material from the collection. Permission to publish extensive excerpts, or material in its entirety, will be referred to the Ford Foundation.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Ford Foundation archive was deposited at the RAC in 2011. Ford Foundation records, correspondence, reports, program files, and officers' papers were transferred to and accessioned by the RAC beginning in 2011.

A later set of Ghebre Selassie Mehreteab Staff Subject Files was transferred to the RAC in 2019 and ingested by the RAC as Accession 2019:108. This accession was incorporated into the collection during processing in January 2020.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: Collection was initially processed to Level 2: Minimal Processing in 2013. A later set of Ghebre Selassie Mehreteab Staff Subject Files was transferred to the RAC in 2019 (Accession 2019:108) and was incorporated into the collection. The entire collection was processed to Level 3: Standard Processing by Darren Young in January 2020.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Collection consists of two series. The correspondence files in the first series are arranged chronologically, and an inconsistent alphabetical arrangement was imposed by the records' creators on the community development corporation grants in the second series.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Collection contains the office files Ghebre Selassie Mehreteab created during his time as a Program Officer in the Ford Foundation's Urban Poverty Program. It consists of two types of files. The first group of files contain Mehreteab's correspondence from the years 1981 to 1985. The second group of files contain Recommended Grant Action records (RGAs) and related materials for the various community development corporations (CDCs) the Urban Poverty Program supported during the 1980s. Mehreteab and his successor Craig Howard oversaw grants concerned with economic development, manpower development, housing, historic preservation, commercial revitalization, political empowerment, community development strategies, and community development information sharing services.

The collection originally consisted only of Mehreteab's correspondence, but another set of Mehreteab's office files was transferred to the RAC in 2019. These files were the CDC RGAs. They were incorporated into the collection as a separate series.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Ghebre Selassie Mehreteab has been involved in the areas of community development and housing for several decades. From 1981 to 1987, he served as a Program Officer in the Ford Foundation's Urban Poverty Program where he managed grants to community development corporations (CDCs). He cofounded the NHP Foundation in 1989 and served as Chief Executive Officer until 2009.

Mehreteab was born in 1949 in Asmara, Eritrea. He graduated from Haverford College in 1972. Before joining the Ford Foundation, he worked with different community organizations in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania and served as an associate director of the New World Foundation.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: Open for research. Brittle or damaged items are available at the discretion of RAC.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Series contains the correspondence Ghebre Selassie Mehreteab created during his time as a Program Officer in the Ford Foundation's Urban Poverty Program. The correspondence discusses community economic development grant requests, grant recommendations, current grantees, site visits to grantees, trips, and meeting s. A number of documents concern the community development corporation (CDC) training workshops the Ford Foundation organized. Mehreteab chiefly corresponded with grantees and potential grantees, Urban Poverty Program Officer in Charge Bernard McDonald and other Ford Foundation staff members, and other individuals involved with community economic development.
The material in the series was created between 1981 and 1985. The series does not include Mehreteab's correspondence from his last years at the Ford Foundation.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Files in the series chiefly consist of Recommended Grant Action records (RGAs) for the various community development corporations (CDCs) and other organizations involved with community economic development that the Ford Foundation supported during the 1980s. Some files include correspondence, memos, reports, and other types of materials in addition to a RGA or RGAs. There are some reports about the Foundation's support for CDCs at the beginning of the series as well as a file filled with program action forms and grant recommendations at the end of the series. The CDCs and other organizations that the Foundation supported pursued projects and initiatives related to economic development, manpower development, housing, historic preservation, commercial revitalization, political empowerment, community development strategies, and community development information sharing services.
The series contains RGAs for the CDC grants Ghebre Selassie Mehreteab managed but also RGAs for the grants that Mehreteab's successor Craig Howard oversaw.
